THE IDEA: the illusions are played BY THE BAND, not by a pad behind it.
- THE STAIR (0:19): a line over the low chug climbs the scale an octave every bar and never gets higher. Four guitars a side play it an octave apart, each fading in at the bottom and out at the top. Every bar is the same bar; every bar starts higher than the last.
- THE TURN (1:17): the low chug at three speeds at once, all speeding up; the fastest fades out as a slower one fades in. Faster and faster, never faster. The kit holds the bar, and every fourth bar line they are together again.
- THE DESCENT (1:55): the stair downwards and all of it: the whole riff a step lower every bar. A tuning that keeps dropping.
- THE POLE (2:53): a breath. One chord through a filter that climbs for ever, and a bass that is only its overtones.
- BOTH (3:22): pitch and speed rise together, like a tape speeding up, under a riser that never arrives. It stops dead.
- THE SUMMIT (4:02): a bar of nothing, then the first bars again, exactly. After all that climbing the band is where it started.

v29, THE RIGHT HAND GOES WITH THE TAPE (section w8, 3:21.6-3:50.4, 'both': the one window of the nine that no round had focused). LISTEN FOR 3:21.6, the china: it no longer keeps eighths over the guitars, it speeds up with them, for twelve bars, and is never faster; the snare stays on two and four under it. Not checked by ear; everything below is measured or reasoned.
WHY. 'Both' is the song's last illusion: pitch and speed rise together, 'as a tape speeding up does'. A tape that speeds up takes the cymbals with it. Here the drummer's right hand kept plain eighths on the china for the whole passage, 300 ms apart from first stroke to last, while six guitars sped up round it: the one part in the passage saying that nothing is getting faster. (Harry on the turn, 17 Nov: 'Faster and faster'.)
WHAT CHANGED. Only the china's eighths in bars 84 to 96: 95 strokes go and 400 come. The china plays the riff's own strokes at all three of the guitars' speeds, each under the same bell as its guitar: one voice fading in from half speed (462 ms apart, to 307), one doubling at full level (295 ms to 152: the eighth becomes the sixteenth), one from the sixteenth towards the thirty-second as it fades out (149 ms to 86). Each voice goes on into the next four bars twice as fast as it began: a Risset rhythm on one cymbal. Every one of the 400 falls on a stroke of the guitar at that speed, and the accents are the riff's (3 3 2), which plain eighths never said. A bar that had 8 strokes has 27, 29, 18 and 22 within 9 dB of full, through each cycle.
WHAT DID NOT. The left hand and the foot keep the clock: the snare on two and four, the bass four in a bar, the crash on each four-bar line (3:21.6, 3:31.2), the kick, every guitar, the three leads, the held string, the gong. At 3:50.4 the hand leaves for the gong as before (v19): the last four bars have no china. So the kit is in two: a hand with the tape and a hand with the clock, and the bar can still be counted.
ONE FIND ON THE WAY: one kit piece on one track is one voice. Written on the cymbal's own track the same strokes read 2 to 15 dB LOWER alone, bar by bar: each quiet stroke of the fast voice cut the ring of a loud one. So the three voices are three tracks (tape0, tape1, tape2), copies of the cymbal's own strip. It is on the sounds board for anyone layering a cymbal.

THE ILLUSION HOLDS (tools/endless.py on the three tracks, a four-bar cycle): the three cycles within 0.3 dB of each other; inside a cycle the level within 0.5 dB of its mean and 0.9 at the wrap; brightness 0.00 octaves a cycle; the notes the same in every cycle but two (the bar line the gong has taken).
